newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SCA sees lower prices on pulp, recycling.
newsitem.headline: SCA sees lower prices on pulp, recycling.

text.p: Swedish forestry company Svenska Cellulosa Aktiebolaget (SCA) Managing Director Sverker Martin-Lof said on Thursday the price trend for pulp and recycling paper was more likely to be down than up.
"Right now the trend is more downwards than upwards...the tendency is for price decreases for pulp, at least for hardwood," Martin-Lof told a news conference.
On other points he was relatively optimistic for 1997.
"Most of the price pressure is hopefully behind us," Martin-Lof said.

With kraftliner paper, on which a stronger dollar usually has a favourable effect, Martin-Lof said price increases can be expected quite soon. For newsprint there are signals of improvement on the U.S. market.
"We hope that a price increase is ahead (in the U.S.)...In Europe it will probably take until the second half of 1997 before any price movements are possible," Martin-Lof said.
He was also optimistic about price increases for LWC (light-weight coated magazine paper) and SC (uncoated magazine paper) during 1997.
